ALGEBRA / MEASURABLE RECONSTRUCTION
Worker: algebra_proof_recon. Independent of the current scouts and blind reviewer.
Status: exact conditional theorem with elementary proof; external validation and
historical priority not established. The finite-color extraction is an independently
reconstructed extension of ASTRA N252/N253, not a new claim of its authorship.

MAIN THEOREM (premise-compatible binary weak-Pinsker consequence).
Let G0 be a countable group and F a finite field of characteristic two. Suppose
a,b in F[G0] satisfy ab=1 and ba!=1. Write |F|=2^d, M=2^d-1, and set
                    G=(G0 x C_M) * Z.
Then, with uniform Haar measure, the binary Bernoulli G-action X=F2^G has
arbitrarily large finite-entropy direct Bernoulli factors. More explicitly there
are an integer m>=1 and a standard probability-measure-preserving G-system R
such that X ~=_G X^2 x R, and for every n>=1,
                    X ~=_G X^n x R^(n-1).
Consequently h_WP(G acting on F2^G)=infinity. If G0 is finitely presented, so is G.
The same action has Rokhlin entropy at most log(2), since its one-coordinate
binary partition is generating. This finite bound is immediate and does not
use the more delicate strict supremal bound in ASTRA N166.
No statement here asserts X ~=_G X^2, Bernoullicity of R, torsion-freeness of G,
or the analogous conclusion for the original group G0.

The algebraic premise is sufficient; it is not proved in this note. In particular
the current OpenAI Family 197 comparator supplies this precise type of premise
as its stated target but its comparator file itself contains sorry. Verification
of an OAI implementation, and verification of the underlying group construction,
are independent obligations not performed by this worker.

1. PRIME-FIELD CORNER TRANSFER.

The group algebra F2[C_M] is A=F2[t]/(t^M-1). Choose a generator alpha of F^*.
Its minimal polynomial f over F2 has degree d, since alpha generates the whole
field. It divides t^M-1. This polynomial is square-free, because M is odd and
its derivative is t^(M-1), coprime to t^M-1. Write t^M-1=f h. By the Chinese
remainder theorem,
                   A ~= F2[t]/f x F2[t]/h.
Here the second factor may be the zero ring when M=1. Let e correspond to (1,0).
Then e^2=e and eA is a copy of F. Let iota:F -> A be its embedding; iota(1)=e.
Coefficientwise extension gives an injective ring homomorphism
             io

PHASE C CROSS-AUDIT ADDENDUM
Reviewer: algebra_blind_review. Date: 2026-10-09.

The coordinator expressly authorized exposure to algebra_proof_recon/PROOF.txt after the independent derivation had been recorded. The independent report remains byte-for-byte unchanged, SHA256 85594c4e6673b46ffb4c8d7f9df9ef164f2dc11077a536baef09810f41310cfd. This addendum is a comparison, not a second blind reconstruction.

Reviewed candidate: work/agents/algebra_proof_recon/PROOF.txt, 323 numbered lines, SHA256 887cda04b08524963fdf4216d505d00c47272abe6800a94e58e3cd54c4572e15. A byte-identical owned snapshot is candidate_PROOF_reviewed_snapshot.txt. All line references below refer to this version.

SCOPED VERDICT

I found no mathematical flaw in the main chain, lines 7-203: finite characteristic-two field witness -> scalar binary witness by a central CRT corner -> free-product defect with trivial action kernel -> finite-power exact product-Haar splitting -> binary Bernoulli action with infinite weak Pinsker entropy. This agrees with and extends the independent argument I supplied before exposure. It is an internally checked conditional theorem, not external validation, not a verified concrete witness, and not a priority certificate.

One definite bibliographic correction is needed at lines 297-300: the paper Superrigidity, measure equivalence, and weak Pinsker entropy is by Lewis Bowen and Robin D. Tucker-Drob, not Bowen, Hoff, and Ioana. The linked paper gives the intended definition, so this attribution error does not damage the proof.

1. FINITE-FIELD / BINARY CORNER TRANSFER: LINES 31-53

The calculation is valid. Let F=F_(2^d), M=2^d-1, and alpha generate F^*. Then F2[alpha]=F, so the minimal polynomial f has degree d. Since alpha^M=1, f divides t^M-1. M is odd, so the derivative is t^(M-1), which has no common factor with t^M-1. Thus f and h=(t^M-1)/f are coprime. CRT gives F2[C_M] ~= F2[t]/(f) x F2[t]/(h). Identifying the first factor with F through evaluation at alpha produces a central idempotent e and a nonunital map into the full ring iota:F->eA with iota(1)=e. This is precisely the corner structure needed; silently treating iota as unital into A would fail, but the candidate does not do so.

Coefficientwise extension is injective because the F2-vector space decomposes over distinct G0 coordinates; multiplying group terms introduces no extra twist since C_M commutes w
